text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE NEWS
- A special committee of the National Assembly (lower house) on Kashmir has turned down the proposal to open trade with India till the resolution of all outstanding issues.
- Pakistan has agreed with the International Monetary Fund to bring the budget deficit down to four percent of GDP by the year 2000.

- The leader of a Shi'ite religious party Allama Syed Sajjid Ali Naqvi demanded that the Chief Minister of Punjab province Shahbaz Sharif resign owing to his failure to control sectarian killings in the province
THE NATION
- The government has decided to sack 2,000 employees of Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) allegedly involved in corruption.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif chaired a meeting to review the law and order situation and recent incidents of sectarian killings in Punjab province.
DAWN
- A larger bench of the Supreme Court comprising three or more judges will conduct hearings on the killings in Karachi, Chief Justice of Pakistan Sajjad Ali Shah said.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif chaired a meeting which discussed the economic situation and expressed satisfaction over the revenue and expenditure position of the government.
- Pakistan and Iran will begin extensive talks in Tehran today on diplomatic efforts to bring peace in Afghanistan through intra-Afghan dialogue, diplomatic sources said.
- The Pakistan Flour Mills Association's Punjab province branch has again increased the price of wheat flour by 0.40 rupees.

- Hamidullah Kansi, elder brother of Mir Aimal Kansi, made a dramatic appearance in the Fairfax Court, U.S., and was cordoned off from the media by security staff and defence lawyers against his will.
- The central bank may increase the mark-up (interest rate) on agricultrural production loans by 0.5 or 1.0 percent, senior bankers said.
- The $500 million 470-megawatt Liberty power plant is in jeeopardy as the government declined to supply it with gas despite the fact that foreign investors offered a lower tariff.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The Privatisation Commission has finalised the schedule for the sale of Ravi Rayon Ltd and a unit of Federal Chemical and Ceramics Corporation Ltd through an open auction.
- The owner of the Tawakal Group of Industries, Abdul Qadir Tawakal, agreed to deposit 2.03 billion rupees in treasury after confessing his crime of defrauding the national exchequer.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
